Spy Photos: 2027 or 2028 Land Rover Range Rover Reveals New Details As It Starts Losing Camouflage
26 photos
Photo: Baldauf
Land Rover is much busier than its JLR sibling Jaguar, which recently announced the Type 01 full-size EV liftback sedan model, as it constantly takes care of its most popular lines – Defender and Range Rover.
Just recently, the premium British specialty automaker revealed the Defender Alasia Pack in Europe, aiming for a touch of Cyprus Copper, and also revealed that customers may now ask for a spare wheel delete on the Defender 90 to enhance visibility and tight-space maneuvering.
The company is also joining forces with Stellantis to start manufacturing Land Rover products in America to escape the grueling tariffs, with the rumor mill claiming they know that the Defender will be the first adopted child of the new family partnerships, with a reported pickup truck versions coming from a US location of Stellantis. Oh, and there’s also the ‘baby’ Defender in the making, an EV compact model, apparently.
Now, let’s talk about Range Rover, which has two new members in the family: the Range Rover Electric and the Range Rover Sport Electric . But wait, there's more – Land Rover has officially teased the upcoming introduction of a third electric model that will also be a hybrid in the near future: the Range Rover GT, which is more like a liftback sedan grand tourer than a regular crossover.
Anyway, according to our spy photographer partners, on top of that Land Rover is also testing the mid-cycle refresh procedure for the Range Rover flagship, and it’s potentially set to arrive for its gala presentation early next year. All those things considered, it’s no surprise that our spies have caught the mighty RR shedding some of its camouflage during prototype testing.
The example caught here (or examples) was dwelling at and around the Nürburgring Nordschleife, as we can clearly see it going all-out on the Green Hell (with a cockpit roll cage!) and then relaxing to or back from the testing center in the German town. “The new Range Sport facelift was already spotted in July with less camouflage, and now the Range Rover facelift has finally been revealed as well,” says our spy.
Now, the “thick plastic camouflage has been removed from the front, and the new grille and bumper are clearly visible. At the rear, the bumper has also been redesigned around the horizontal rear fog light and the horizontal reverse light strip. Updates are also expected in the interior.” There are some things that won’t change – the powertrains.
As such, the mid-cycle refresh of the big Range Rover is expected soon, with minor changes to the exterior and potential upgrades for the interior, but most likely the drivetrains will remain the same, with gasoline, diesel, plug-in hybrid, and battery electric versions.
